mathematical_derivation.face_conductance_formula: C_f = 2 * k_f * (dy / dx) * thickness = 2 * k_f * (1.0) * 1.0 = 2 * k_f [W/K]
mathematical_derivation.face_conductance_resolution_dependence: O(1) - Exactly resolution invariant on square grid cells
mathematical_derivation.discrete_boundary_gradient: dT/dn_f = (T_P - T_b) / (dx / 2) = 2 * N * (T_P - T_b) [K/m] -> Scales as O(1/dx) = O(N)
mathematical_derivation.accumulated_flux_error_formula: Delta_Q = sum_{f=1}^{4N} C_f * (T_P - T_b - Delta_T_exact) = O(N) for coherent bias
mathematical_derivation.physical_root_cause: The 11.3x increase in absolute boundary flux imbalance from 359 W at 32x32 to 4,054 W at 256x256 is an expected mathematical scaling consequence of discrete gradient evaluation on cell-centred grids. Because face conductance C_f = 2*k is constant, the perimeter face count grows as 4*N (128 -> 1024), and discrete temperature gradients scale as 1/dx = N, any unprojected point error in boundary temperature (which remains bounded between 2.36 K and 2.81 K across all resolutions) is integrated across 4*N faces. The empirical log-log scaling exponent of flux imbalance is alpha = 1.16, closely matching the theoretical O(N) prediction (alpha = 1.0). In contrast, temperature RMSE increases by only 0.45 K across an 8x grid refinement, confirming that the physical temperature field does NOT deteriorate.

conclusions.recommended_mitigation: For production hybrid inference at fine resolutions (>= 128x128), acceptance screening should NOT use unnormalized absolute flux imbalance with fixed thresholds calibrated at 32x32. Instead, it must use either: (1) DiscreteBoundaryCorrection projection to enforce exact face consistency, or (2) resolution-scaled threshold I_abs_thresh(N) = I_0 * (N / 32), or (3) normalized relative imbalance.
